title: The matching-section sheaf equalizer realizes a formal gluing chart
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, $C$ its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ the complement of its closed point. Let $q:Y\to U$ and $s:E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be finite morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $D$ be completion overlap data with matching ring $B$, base map $a:A\to B$, model map $m:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and punctured map $p:Y\to m^{-1}(U)$ [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. Fix $t\in\mathbb N$, $g:\operatorname{Fin}t\to A$ with $(g_j)=\mathfrak m$, and $i\in\operatorname{Fin}t$. Put $W=(m|_U)^{-1}((U\to\operatorname{Spec}A)^{-1}(D(g_i)))$. Let $\rho:B\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)$ be restriction after the affine global-section isomorphism, and $\psi:\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(p^{-1}(W),\mathcal O)$ pullback along $p|_W$. Give $B$ its $A$-action via $a$, and the latter chart section ring its $A$-action via $\psi\rho a$. There exist formal gluing data $X$ for $A\to C$ and $g$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], an $A$-linear equivalence $b:H^0(X)\simeq B$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0], and an $A$-linear equivalence $c:X.M_i\simeq\Gamma(p^{-1}(W),\mathcal O)$ from its chart module (viewed by restriction of scalars), such that $\psi(\rho(b(h)))=c(h_i)$ for every compatible tuple $h\in H^0(X)$. This asserts a geometric identification, with no denominator-lifting or localization-surjectivity assertion.

source.place: Tag 0BLH, proof, first two paragraphs (the affine chart datum); Tag 05EL, displayed definition of H0. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BLH and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05EL.

proof.text: For each g_j let Y_j be the inverse image under q of D(g_j) in U. Since the g_j span the maximal ideal, these principal opens cover U. Finite q makes each Y_j affine, and finite s makes E affine. Set the chart modules to their global section rings with their A[1/g_j]-actions, and the prime module to Gamma(E) with its completion action. Use affine principal-open localization and the affine tensor-product description of base change to identify the prime localizations with the extended chart modules via D.overlapIso. Restrictions to double charts give alpha_overlap. On numerators the square and cocycle identities are functoriality of restriction; the fact that overlapIso is over Spec C gives alpha_smul. These are exactly the fields of FormalGlueing.Data.

Given h in H0, glue its chart sections to a global section of Y. Its prime/chart equations assert equality with its prime coordinate on the overlap; check on the principal-open cover and use sheaf separatedness. This pair is an element of the explicit pullback matching ring. Conversely, restrict a matching pair to all Y_j and retain its completed coordinate. The restrictions satisfy both compatibility equations. Sheaf uniqueness and pullback uniqueness show that the two operations are inverse; they preserve the structural A-actions. Thus they give the linear equivalence b from H0 to the matching ring.

By puncturedMap_over and inverse-image functoriality, the chart Y_i identifies canonically with puncturedMap inverse image of W. Pullback of sections along this restriction isomorphism gives c. Functoriality of appTop and the Spec-Gamma adjunction identify psi(rho(b(h))) with c of the i-coordinate: the first pullback projection of b(h) is the glued Y section, and its restriction is the i-coordinate. The same equality on structural base elements identifies the A-action with multiplication by psi(rho(baseMap(a))), proving A-linearity for the explicitly stated action. Nilpotent generators give zero chart modules; empty U retains only the prime coordinate, with all chart restrictions zero.

from.place: The completion overlap matching algebra used in the punctured finite-model input; geometric affine chart/equalizer identification before denominator lifting, steps 1 and 2 of lem-sbc-punctured-matching-chart-power-lift.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_formalGlueingData_matching_chart
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens}
    (hU : ∀ x : Spec (.of A), x ∈ U ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme} [IsFinite q]
    {E : Scheme.{u}} {s : E ⟶ Spec
      (.of (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A))} [IsFinite s]
    (D : CompletionGluingData A U q E s) (t : ℕ) (g : Fin t → A)
    (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (i : Fin t) :
    let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A
    let φ := algebraMap A C
    let W := (D.modelMap ∣_ U) ⁻¹ᵁ (U.ι ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g i))
    let ρ := ((ΓSpecIso D.matchingRing).inv ≫
      (W.ι ≫ (D.modelMap ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).appTop).hom
    let ψ := (D.puncturedMap ∣_ W).appTop.hom
    letI : Algebra A D.matchingRing := D.baseMap.hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra A Γ((D.puncturedMap ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, ⊤) :=
      ((ψ.comp ρ).comp D.baseMap.hom).toAlgebra
    ∃ (X : FormalGlueing.Data.{u, u, u} φ g)
      (b : FormalGlueing.h0 φ g X ≃ₗ[A] D.matchingRing)
      (c : FormalGlueing.piece (g i) (X.M i) ≃ₗ[A]
        Γ((D.puncturedMap ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, ⊤)),
      ∀ h, ψ (ρ (b h)) = c (h.val.2 i)
